title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: Documents in Force on a Booking
content:
`Bills of Lading and Transport Documents` are counted booking by booking. This page defines when a document is "in force" on a booking, how many may be in force together, and what becomes of a document whose booking is cancelled.

## Clauses

1. **Document in force.** A transport document is in force in every status except voided. Draft, approved, issued, surrendered, released and accomplished documents are all in force.
2. **One per booking.** A booking carries no more than one document in force. A fresh draft may be generated for a booking only if each document previously created for that booking now stands voided. The test rests on the line's own records of the documents held against that booking and the status each one shows; a caller's account of earlier documents does not substitute for those records.
3. **Switch bill exception.** A switch bill is the only case where a booking acquires a second document. Its draft may be created while the document being exchanged is in the status surrendered. When the switch bill is issued, the exchanged document is voided, and from that moment the booking once again has only one document in force.
4. **Cancelled booking.** When a booking is cancelled, a document of that booking that is still a draft or approved is voided. An issued document on a cancelled booking does not arise, because no cargo is ever shipped under a cancelled booking.

## Input, judgement, output

| Documents already on the booking | New draft for the booking |
|---|---|
| None | May be created |
| All of them voided | May be created |
| At least one draft, approved, issued, released or accomplished | Not created |
| One surrendered document, and the new draft is a switch bill in exchange for it | May be created |

## Basis Q&A

**A booking already carries an approved draft. Can a second, parallel draft be opened for it?** No. An approved draft is in force, and while it is in force no other ordinary draft exists for that booking.

**Between the switch bill's draft and its issue, the booking shows two documents. Is that a breach?** No. That overlap is the permitted switch bill exception; it closes when the switch bill is issued and the exchanged document is voided.

**Hypothetical case.** A booking is cancelled while its document sits in the status approved. The document is voided; it never reached issue, so nothing about originals arises.
